supersedes.why: v0.1 bound this synapse class to a depression-only Tsodyks-Markram rule with Nagel, Hong and Wilson's published utilisation of 0.22 and recovery constant of 893 ms. It faced two independent external tests and passed neither, and the second failure was structural rather than numerical: the measured paired-pulse ratios exceed one at three of five intervals and decrease with interval, and a single depleting resource can do neither at any parameter setting. No refitting could repair it, which is why this is a new registry rather than new values in the old one.
supersedes.v0_1_is_preserved_unchanged: Its failing predictions, its two external tests and its verdicts stay exactly as recorded. Nothing here rewrites them.
supersedes.what_the_successor_search_also_refuted: The minimal repair does not work. A family that keeps the published utilisation and recovery constant exactly as v0.1 registers them and adds the missing facilitation is capped at a paired-pulse ratio of 1.388 by that pinning, against a measured 10 ms cohort mean of 1.5139, and it lands outside the fit set's own interval. So the diagnosis recorded on 2026-09-09 -- a missing mechanism rather than wrong parameters -- was half right. The mechanism was missing and the parameters are also wrong for this synapse as these recordings measure it.
supersedes.what_the_project_actually_has_now: No usable ORN-to-PN short-term-plasticity rule at all. v0.1 is refuted and these two candidates are unvalidated, so the honest position is an empty slot rather than a succession. 'Supersedes' below describes what v0.1's failure forced, not a handover of a working rule.

purpose: To carry a short-term-plasticity rule for the ORN-to-PN synapse that was frozen before it was tested. Both rules below are fitted values, both are frozen with their predictions written down, and their only test is the sealed day-1 and day-0 wild-type cohorts under stage2-stp-developmental-holdout-v1. Until that test returns, this registry awards no tier and is an executable labelled alternative exactly as v0.1 was.

how_these_rules_were_obtained.fit_set: the five wild-type paired-pulse cohort means of Rozenfeld and colleagues' Figure 3D, 2 to 4 days post eclosion, which were opened and scored on 2026-09-09 and are therefore spent

screens.e1: the fitted curve must lie inside the fit set's 95 percent interval at 5 of 5 intervals
screens.e2: the bootstrap 95 percent band on the frozen prediction must be no wider at any interval than the fit set's own 95 percent interval there. This screen carries no threshold of its own: it scales to the data.
screens.e3: every constant a family pins rather than fits must be refitted across its declared sweep and move the five predictions by at most 0.01
screens.reported_not_gating: parameter-level identifiability, the chi-square goodness of fit, the leave-one-interval-out error, and the comparison against Kazama and Wilson's measured release probability
screens.selection: among eligible families the lowest weighted residual is the primary and the fewest parameters is the secondary

selection.primary_rule: lowest weighted residual among eligible families
selection.secondary_rule: fewest parameters among the rest, ties by weighted residual
selection.why: two-timescale-facilitation-free carries the lowest weighted residual of the eligible families and is frozen as the primary. facilitation-depression is frozen alongside it as the secondary so an unseen cohort can adjudicate between them, which the fit set cannot.

how_these_rules_were_obtained.why_two_rules_are_frozen: The fit set cannot choose between a four-parameter and a five-parameter account of five cohort means. On data the five-parameter family generates it wins 99 times in 100; on data the four-parameter family generates the five-parameter one still wins, because it nests it. That asymmetry is exactly what nesting predicts and it means the fit set is not an arbiter. Both are frozen and an unseen cohort decides. The primary carries the verdict.

the_observation_model.protocol_is_simulated: Twenty pairs at a 5000 ms repetition period, because the methods state that paired-pulse recordings were made at 0.2 Hz with twenty traces averaged per interval. The reported ratio is the mean second response over the mean first across those twenty, and the earlier pairs leave the resource partly depleted. Every prediction in this registry is computed that way. At 1000 ms the correction is about 0.028 in ratio units, larger than that cohort's own standard error, so it is not cosmetic.

rules.title: M4f: M4 with the fast facilitation constant fitted rather than pinned
rules.mechanism: The same two facilitating components as M4 over the same depleting resource, with the fast time constant fitted. It exists so that the decision to pin that constant is itself under test rather than assumed.
rules.provenance_note: Every value is a fitted value, fitted to the wild-type paired-pulse cohort means of Rozenfeld and colleagues' Figure 3D, which were already spent. Not one of them is a measurement of a MaleCNS synapse and not one is taken from a published fit.
rules.what_that_split_means: A parameter in the second list could not be recovered when the family was refitted to data it generated itself at the measured noise level. It is a number the fit needs and the observable does not determine, and quoting it as a measured synaptic property would be an overclaim. The predictions are nevertheless sharp: the bootstrap band on the frozen curve is narrower than the fit set's own interval at every one of the five intervals, which is the eligibility screen this rule had to pass. Unidentifiable parameters with well-determined predictions is the ordinary condition of a mechanistic model fitted to a few summary statistics, and separating the two is the point.

fit_quality_on_the_spent_fit_set.this_is_not_evidence: A chi-square goodness-of-fit p-value on five cohort means is not evidence that a mechanism is right, and a large one is not a virtue. With one residual degree of freedom a p near 0.9 says the residual is SMALLER than chance would give, which is what over-parameterisation looks like, not what a validated model looks like. With zero residual degrees of freedom, as the primary candidate has, no p exists at all. These numbers are reported so the fit can be audited and for no other purpose. Neither a saturated nor a near-saturated fit validates anything, and the earlier prose describing the best-fitting family as 'the best fit of all' invited exactly that reading.

against_the_measured_release_probability.source: Kazama and Wilson 2008, multiple-probability fluctuation analysis
against_the_measured_release_probability.the_tension_is_recorded_not_resolved: Every family that could reproduce this paired-pulse curve needed an effective first-pulse utilisation between 0.07 and 0.13, which is eight to eleven times below the release probability Kazama and Wilson measured at this synapse. Mapping a fitted utilisation onto a per-site release probability needs one vesicle per site and no within-pair recovery, which the v0.1 registry already records as the reason the variance-derived value was not adopted, so this is not a clean contradiction. It is a large unexplained gap and it is recorded here rather than left out. A synapse with a release probability near 0.79 should barely facilitate at all, and these recordings facilitate by fifty per cent at 10 ms.

rules.structural_limits: Five free parameters against five cohort means leaves no residual degrees of freedom, so this family has no goodness-of-fit statistic and cannot be tested in sample at all. Its fast step and fast constant trade off along a ridge, so neither is separately determined by a curve whose shortest interval is 10 ms; what the data determine is the fast component's contribution at that one interval. Its facilitation is additive and has no ceiling of its own, but it multiplies a depleting resource and does not run away in a long train: over 112 pulses at 60 Hz it peaks near 1.4 times the first response at pulse four and falls under three per cent of it by the end.

rules.title: M1: release-probability facilitation over a depleting resource
rules.mechanism: The standard two-state Markram-Tsodyks synapse. Residual calcium raises release probability for tens of milliseconds while the vesicle pool is depleted for hundreds, so a facilitating short interval and a depressing long one arise from one mechanism with two time constants.

rules.structural_limits: The four parameters are in bijection with the four quantities a paired-pulse curve can identify, so nothing here is a fitted direction the observable cannot see. The ceiling of two is approached only as the resting utilisation goes to zero, where the response itself vanishes.

flat_null.why_it_is_here: A model that cannot beat a horizontal line on the holdout has not been tested by the holdout. This level is frozen with everything else so the comparison on unseen cohorts is between two predictions made in advance.

engine_coverage.numpy_circuit_runner: not implemented for these families; only the v0.1 depression-only rule has a runner
engine_coverage.why_this_is_recorded_now: Neither frozen rule can yet be executed inside a circuit simulation. They exist as closed-form and state-machine predictors of a paired-pulse ratio. Wiring them into the runners is work that should not be done until the holdout says whether either of them survives.

validation_status: FROZEN, UNVALIDATED, AND NOW WITHOUT A REMAINING HOLDOUT as of 2026-09-10. This file is a candidate-family set, not a rule. Its registered developmental holdout returned NO VERDICT because the primary cohort was the training set. Its registered train experiment is VOID because the arrays it scored are per-pulse latencies rather than amplitudes, which the intake mis-described on 2026-09-09. No validation tier is awarded and none may be cited. The corpus contains no ORN-to-PN train amplitude series at all, so the pinned recovery constant is unmeasurable from it rather than merely unmeasured, and advancing this rule requires a different dataset rather than a different contract. The release-probability incompatibility recorded above is untouched by any of this and remains the sharpest open problem.
what_this_registry_does_not_do: It does not reinstate the retired synaptic leg of the Stage 2 gate, which needs unitary waveforms this repository does not ship. The gate stays at v4 and 0 of 3.
It does not resolve edge sign, which is ND-10 and stays unresolved wherever receptor evidence is absent.
It does not predict trains, latencies, jitter, absolute amplitudes, miniature EPSCs or any perturbation.
It does not apply to ORN-to-local-neuron synapses, which are a different class with no registered parameters at all.

It carries no glomerulus specificity. The recordings pool an unstated mixture of glomeruli through the GH146-QF driver, which labels about 60 per cent of projection neurons, while Nagel and colleagues fitted DM6 and VM2.

holdout.why: The registered primary cohort was void. The Fig3J wild-type arrays are bit-identical to the arrays these rules were fitted to: the repository ships the same wild-type reference in both figure files, and the published legends give it the same animal counts in both, which was noticed before the run and not acted on. Scoring it scored the training set. The artifact's PASSED verdict applied the registered rule faithfully to a cohort that was not a holdout, and it is superseded by the contract's execution record.

what_the_one_genuine_cohort_returned.cohort: wild type, 0 days post eclosion, Fig3H, 20 to 21 animals per interval
what_the_one_genuine_cohort_returned.registered_role: secondary; declared in advance not to enter the verdict
what_the_one_genuine_cohort_returned.A1_prediction_inside_the_measurement_err: NO VERDICT. The frozen primary's prediction does lie inside all five intervals, but the 10 ms and 30 ms half-widths are about 0.19 and 0.17 against the registered 0.15 power limit, leaving three scorable intervals against a registered minimum of four. An interval that wide would contain many wrong predictions too, which is what the limit is for.
what_the_one_genuine_cohort_returned.A2_better_than_a_frozen_constant: PASSED, and it is the one substantive registered result, but the margin should not be quoted without its null. On 21 animals neither rule had seen, the primary's weighted residual is 1.493 against the frozen constant's 38.612. That constant sits at 0.9785 while the cohort means span 0.92 to 1.46, so any curve with roughly the right shape beats it comfortably; the factor of 26 measures how much structure the data have, not how good the model is. What the result does establish is the thing worth establishing: a model frozen with its numbers written down beforehand outperformed a null also frozen beforehand, on animals it had not seen, under a criterion fixed in advance. That is a first for this project and it is not a tier.
what_the_one_genuine_cohort_returned.A3_shape: PASSED, 4 of 4 adjacent directions, and the frozen constant passes it too, so it carries little.
what_the_one_genuine_cohort_returned.did_it_separate_the_two_frozen_rules: No. The four-parameter single-facilitation rule does marginally better here than the five-parameter two-timescale rule, 1.279 against 1.493, which points the opposite way from the fit set where the two-timescale family was better by a factor of hundreds. The two curves differ by up to 0.075 at 100 ms, above the 0.02 separability limit, but that cohort's 100 ms half-width is 0.12. One cohort of this size cannot tell them apart, and neither rule may be preferred over the other on this evidence.

holdout.what_this_registry_may_now_claim: That its primary candidate, frozen with its parameters and its five predictions written down before the cohort was opened, tracks an unseen wild-type cohort better than a frozen constant does, under a criterion fixed in advance. The null is weak and the margin should always be reported with it. It is the first time any dynamical model in this project has been frozen and then beaten any null on unseen animals, and it is not a validation tier: the registered experiment returns NO VERDICT because its primary cohort was the training set, and the criterion that asks whether the predictions land inside the measurement error returned NO VERDICT on power.
what_it_may_not_claim: A passed holdout. The experiment as registered returns NO VERDICT.
Any validation tier. V0 remains the only supported tier in the project.
That the two-timescale mechanism is established. The one genuine cohort mildly favours the simpler rule and cannot separate them.
That the fit-set agreement means anything. The fit set was spent before the fit.
That the 26-fold margin over the frozen constant is a strong result. The constant is a weak null against data with this much structure.

what_this_file_is: A frozen CANDIDATE-FAMILY SET, not a rule. It holds two mechanisms that survived a screen on spent data, frozen with their predictions written down. Neither has passed a holdout, the project's registered test of them returned NO VERDICT, and one genuine unseen cohort could not separate them. Nothing here may be used as the ORN-to-PN plasticity rule in a simulation, and the file was renamed from a v0.2 registry to a candidate set on 2026-09-10 because the earlier name implied a successor that had replaced something.

the_release_probability_incompatibility.status: The sharpest result this exercise produced, and it is a problem for every candidate rather than a property of one.
the_release_probability_incompatibility.the_bound: Take one homogeneous pool of release sites, each holding at most one vesicle, each releasing with probability p at rest; let the second pulse release with any probability up to one, and let a site that released be unavailable until it recovers. Then the paired-pulse ratio is (p2/p1)(1 - p1 exp(-dt/tau)), which is at most (1 - p exp(-dt/tau))/p. The bound is generous by construction: it allows instantaneous facilitation to certainty, no desensitisation, no postsynaptic saturation and an unchanged quantal size.

the_numbers.measured_release_probability: 0.79 plus or minus 0.02, Kazama and Wilson 2008, multiple-probability fluctuation analysis, uniform across glomeruli
the_numbers.insensitive_to_the_recovery_constant: At a 20000 ms recovery constant instead of 893 ms the ceiling is 0.2663 and the cap is 0.3979. The conclusion does not depend on the pinned value.

the_release_probability_incompatibility.what_it_means: At least one of three things is false: that the resting release probability at this synapse is near 0.79; that the Rozenfeld paired-pulse ratios measure the same quantity at the same synapse; or that a single homogeneous pool describes it. No facilitation mechanism can reconcile the first and second, because the bound already grants facilitation everything it could ask for.
the_release_probability_incompatibility.which_is_most_likely_wrong_and_why_it_ma: The bound holds for any distribution of per-site release probabilities, because the first response is N E[p] q and the second is at most N (1 - E[p] exp(-dt/tau)) q, so only the mean enters and the spread cancels. Heterogeneity is therefore not available as a resolution. What survives is: (a) the mean release probability is not 0.79 at this synapse under these conditions -- multiple-probability fluctuation analysis assumes a uniform release probability and heterogeneity is a known source of bias in it, so heterogeneity remains relevant as a reason to distrust the number rather than as a mechanism, and the direction of that bias should be verified against the method literature rather than assumed; (b) the two measurements are of different quantities or preparations, Kazama and Wilson having stimulated the antennal nerve at 0.033 Hz while Rozenfeld and colleagues used minimal stimulation of ORN axons at 0.2 Hz through a driver labelling about sixty per cent of projection neurons; (c) the one-vesicle-per-site assumption fails, through multivesicular release or through recruitment of release sites that were not available on the first pulse -- this is the only surviving presynaptic MECHANISM, since it is the assumption the bound actually needs; or (d) postsynaptic saturation, which raises a measured ratio and is recorded in VAL-02.
the_release_probability_incompatibility.the_consequence_for_this_candidate_set: Unchanged in substance and changed in its reason. The parallel-release-components family was excluded on E2, because its frozen prediction band was wider than the data at 10 and 30 ms, and that exclusion stands as a statement about what five summary statistics can pin down. What is now withdrawn is the claim that it was nonetheless the mechanistically indicated family because it encodes heterogeneity: heterogeneity does not produce paired-pulse facilitation and does not reconcile the two measurements. That family's facilitating component works because it facilitates, not because the pool is mixed, and its standing is exactly what E2 says it is.
the_release_probability_incompatibility.the_escape_hatch_that_must_be_named: Postsynaptic saturation raises a measured paired-pulse ratio, so if the recordings saturate, the true presynaptic ratio is lower than 1.5139 and the bound is less badly violated. VAL-02 records that mechanism. It is weak here because minimal stimulation is designed to stay off the saturating part of the curve, which was established on 2026-09-09, but it is not zero and it is the one route by which a high release probability could survive.
the_release_probability_incompatibility.computed_by: flysim.stp_families.single_pool_paired_pulse_ceiling and maximum_single_pool_release_probability, both asserted in the test suite
the_release_probability_incompatibility.the_bound_is_general_over_heterogeneity: Take any distribution of per-site release probabilities. R1 = N E[p] q and R2 is at most N (1 - E[p] exp(-dt/tau)) q, so the ceiling is (1 - E[p] exp(-dt/tau)) / E[p]: the mean alone, with the spread cancelling. Verified analytically and by a site-by-site Monte Carlo in the test suite.
the_release_probability_incompatibility.heterogeneity_does_not_help_and_the_earl: An earlier version of this record said a heterogeneous population facilitates on a paired pulse with no change in per-site probability, because the first pulse preferentially depletes the high-probability sites and the survivors are the low-probability ones. That is backwards. The survivors do carry the second response and they carry LESS of it, because the sites removed were the ones contributing most: with no facilitation the ratio is 1 - c (E[p] + Var[p]/E[p]), strictly below the homogeneous 1 - c E[p] whenever the variance is positive. Simulated: at E[p] = 0.79 the homogeneous ratio is 0.2188 and a bimodal pool of 0.95 and 0.63 gives 0.1868, with an extreme 1.0-and-0.58 pool giving 0.1636. Heterogeneity makes paired-pulse depression worse, never better.

the_train_experiment_was_void.why: Per-pulse evoked-EPSC LATENCY, in sample units. The row mean of each all_flies_<f>_control array equals that file's mean_rise_time_<f>_control exactly -- ratio 20.000000 with zero spread across all seventeen animals at 1, 10 and 20 Hz, and 5.000000 with zero spread at 60 Hz, which are the sampling rates in samples per millisecond. Converted, the per-animal latencies are 3.9, 4.1, 4.3 and 4.3 ms for the first animal across the four frequencies, which is both the right magnitude for a synaptic latency and the increase with stimulation frequency the paper reports for Figure 3E.
the_train_experiment_was_void.what_it_changes_for_this_registry: There is no unspent wild-type ORN-to-PN amplitude holdout in this corpus, and there never was one. Rozenfeld and colleagues' repository offers, for this synapse: per-animal mean evoked amplitude at 1 Hz in Fig3B, Fig3G and Fig3I, of which Fig3B and Fig3I are bit-identical; paired-pulse ratios in Fig3D, Fig3H and Fig3J, of which Fig3D and Fig3J are bit-identical; miniature EPSC amplitude and frequency in Fig5B; and Bruchpilot puncta in Fig5D. No train amplitude series exists anywhere in it. So the resource recovery constant cannot be measured from this corpus by anyone, the plan to settle it with the trains was built on a mis-read header, and the candidates' pinned constant remains unmeasurable rather than merely unmeasured.
the_train_experiment_was_void.the_corpus_claim_and_its_qualification: A whole-repository structure audit on 2026-09-10 read all 66 MAT files and confirmed that no ORN-to-PN evoked-amplitude train series exists in any of the 61 that could be read. Five could not be read -- three are MATLAB v7.3 and two defeat this project's v5 structure reader -- so the claim covers 61 of 66 files and not the repository. Four of the five belong to odour-response or behaviour figures, which makes an amplitude train series unlikely there, and 'unlikely' is recorded as an open question rather than as a conclusion.
